text.p: SOLIDERE shares rose slightly on Friday on the privately-operated Beirut Secondary Market (BSM).

On the official Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE), only 2,500 Ciments Libanais shares were traded at $1.3125 -- 4.55 percent down on their price on Wednesday when they were last trade on sale of 1,500 shares.

A shares rose to $115.625 from Thursday's $115.25 on the BSM and B shares rose to $117.50 from $117.250. Both shares have been gaining in value since last week, with rises of more than two percent daily before Thursday's close.

Dealers say momentum had been building up on the Beirut equities market because of expectations that SOLIDERE will launch a $150 million GDR issue in mid-October, giving non-Arab investors access to the market for the first time.
SOLIDERE, the company which is rebuilding war-damaged central Beirut, has declined to comment on the report which followed rumours on the Beirut market.
Turnover on the BSM, which trades only SOLIDERE shares, fell to 11,668 shares against 15,460 on Thursday and value was $1,362,200.5 from $1,793,646.75.
The BLOM stock index fell 0.35 percent to 995.54. The LISPI index fell 0.59 percent to 85.13. They covers both markets.

"LISPI moved down 0.59 percent to 85.13 despite an increase in the prices of SOLIDERE A shares to $115.625 and an increase in the SOLIDERE B shares prices to $117.500 as the price of SCL shares fell 4.55 percent to $1.3125," Lebanon Invest Research Company, which compiles the index, said in a bulletin.
There was no trade on the official exchange in any of the three other listed companies: Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic. -Beirut editorial (961 1) 864148 353078 861723
